summary: Mineral County, MT lookout on Ninemile Divide: a 1927 summer post at a camp, a 40-ft pole L-4 tower built 1931 and removed 1964; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Removed in 1964 per firelookout.com; no source describes what remains at the site

events.note: Missoula school principal posted as a summer fire lookout on the divide, at a camp, before the 1931 tower (Missoulian item of July 16, 1927, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Mr. & Mrs. Daniel Demontigny listed as lookout personnel

evidence.supports: listed in Mineral County as a tower, status gone
six miles east-northeast of Superior, Mineral County
July 1927 summer lookout posting on the divide
evidence.quote: is located on the Nine Mile divide in the Superior district as a forest lookout for the summer fire protection

evidence.supports: July 16, 1927 date of the Missoulian item

evidence.quote: principal of the Willard and Franklin schools in Missoula

evidence.supports: spent several days improving the camp
evidence.quote: spent several days in improving the camp.

evidence.supports: built 1931 as a 40-foot pole L-4; removed 1964

sources.title: Ninemile Divide
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (Ron Kemnow), quoting The Missoulian

notes_for_editor: Only two web pages describe this tower. Both agree it was removed, but the 1931 build and 1964 removal dates come from firelookout.com alone. The 1927 item describes a camp and a posting, not a tower, so the story does not say a tower stood then. Two web searches found nothing else about this tower. Stark Mountain on the Lolo is a different lookout on the same divide; search snippets describe it as staffed (not read), so do not mix the two. Elevation 6,857 ft (about 2,090 m) per firelookout.com could fill elevation_m. Record name, county, agency and coordinates match the FFLA list. No photo with an image URL was found.
